title: Public quantized workloads did not show a better prefetch memory frontier
summary: With public chat and recorded agent content, smaller-cache ARC achieved the same memory saving. The candidate missed the matched-ARC 1% chat target, while agent gains varied with generated histories. An eight-budget screen did not extend the useful low-memory range.
scope: RTX 2080 Ti/WSL, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ, FP16, 3.5 GiB CPU KV. Three paired corpus partitions in the translation study; a separate one-partition GPU-budget screen had 14 valid points and two proof-invalid holes.
limitations: Tool observations and wait durations were replayed/simulated rather than produced by live tools. Agent histories differed across arms; no exact-work causal gain. At 672 MiB the candidate consumed only about 3.2% of speculative traffic for its named demand. Strict-invalid points remain excluded.
decision: Right-size the ARC control first. Keep shared-prefix/JIT publication functionality distinct from policy value, and retain reservation waste, preemption, latency and proof failures when considering future designs.

chart.caption: First two are paired geometric changes across three partitions; last two are separate one-pass screen observations. No common uncertainty estimate.
